title: Word-Representability of Shift Graphs
summary: A graph $G=(V,E)$ is word-representable if there exists a word $w$ over the alphabet $V$ such that letters $x$ and $y$ alternate in $w$ if and only if $xy\in E$. For integers $n>k>0 $, the shift graph $G(n,k)$ is the graph whose vertex set consists of all increasing $k$-tuples $(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_k)$ with $1\le x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_k\le n$, where two vertices $(x_1,\dots,x_k)$ and $(y_1,\dots,y_k)$ are adjacent whenever $x_{i+1}=y_i$ for all $1\le i\le k-1$ or $y_{i+1}=x_i$ for all $1\le i\le k-1$.
